plan.why: Dept 3 is the largest dollar gap and was below forecast chain-wide, pointing to a category-level cause; Dept 95 and Dept 72 are the next largest gaps, and Dept 72 stands out because it was flat across all other stores, so it needs a regional or category explanation.

passages.text: Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Similarly, weekly attendance and revenues at Broadway theaters were running ahead of comparable 2011 levels in August and early September but slipped well below year-earlier levels for the third week of the month. Finally, consumer confidence fell in August and was little changed at a low level in September, according to the Conference Board's monthly survey of residents of the Middle Atlantic states (NY, NJ, Pa).

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We had positive comps across all geographies and store formats. During the quarter, we focused on being the destination for back-to-school and Halloween shopping. Our merchants and operators developed a strong cross-functional plan, and I'm pleased with our execution and the sales growth achieved this year. As a reminder, a slightly larger portion of Halloween sales versus last year will fall into the fourth quarter comp period, given how the 4-5-4 calendar falls this year.

report.summary: Store 27 was below the ML forecast in most departments the week ending Sep 14, 2012, and so were most stores in the chain and the other New York stores. The shared pattern points to a wider cause, but no single cause was verified. Electronics is the exception: it was flat across the chain and the region, so its drop looks local to this store.

findings.title: Chain-wide shortfall that week
findings.text: Across all 45 stores, sales were $44,169,616 against a forecast of $46,628,419 (-5.3%), and 36 of 45 stores were below the forecast. The store's own gap is larger than the chain's.

findings.title: New York stores also below forecast
findings.text: The other New York stores were below the ML forecast in most of the flagged departments, including Dept 3 Stationery, Dept 16 Lawn & Garden, Dept 46 Cosmetics and Dept 96 Liquor. This suggests a shared regional factor, but the cause is not identified.

findings.title: Store-wide shortfall across departments
findings.text: Store 27 as a whole was $1,511,915 against a forecast of $1,751,935 (-13.7%), and 60 of its 69 departments were below the ML forecast. A drop this broad points to something affecting the whole store, though the data does not say what.

findings.title: Electronics drop is local to this store
findings.text: Dept 72 Electronics was $15,397 below the ML forecast (-28.4%) here. Across all stores its total was +0.3%, and the other New York stores were not below the forecast, so this drop is not shared and may be local.

findings.title: Regional reports mixed on sales
findings.text: The Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book, published before this week, said "Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August." The Oct 10, 2012 report, published after this week, said "sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts." These are general regional statements and do not name this store or these departments.

departments.what_supports_it: Store 27 was $34,988 below the ML forecast (-59.2%). 43 of 44 other stores were also below the forecast in this department, and all stores together were -34.3%, so the drop is widely shared.

Store 27 was $15,397 below the ML forecast (-28.4%), while all stores together were +0.3% and no other New York store was below the forecast. This points to a local cause at this store, not a wider one.
Store 27 was $7,947 below the ML forecast (-44.6%). 42 of 44 other stores and all 3 other New York stores were also below the forecast in this department.

report.not_found: No report, outside factor or other department data explains the drops in these specific departments; no passage names Store 27, its departments or its stock.

Ask the store about local events, road work or nearby competitor openings that could affect traffic in the week ending Sep 14, 2012.
